sources.entry: MacResourceMonitor - Menu bar CPU monitor to see which process is eating CPU and terminate it directly. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/x0c/MacResourceMonitor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that shows which process is using the most CPU and lets you end it directly, with an optional command-line "mrm doom" mode for quieting a stuck Mac.
summary.what_it_does: Mac Resource Monitor is a menu bar app that shows the CPU and memory hogs on your Mac in a flat table, with human-readable process names. Clicking the menu bar dual ring (outer ring CPU, inner ring memory) opens the table, and each row has an end control that terminates that process. Columns can be sorted by CPU or memory, and a Freeze toggle keeps row order steady while values keep updating. The table also includes a network list showing per-process speed. A command-line interface, "mrm", offers the same table and safety rules; "mrm doom" previews and then ends your own non-system processes, with flags such as --dry-run, --yes, --json and --exclude. The README states that everything stays local with no account or telemetry, and it is distributed via Homebrew cask or a signed, notarized DMG with Sparkle auto-updates.
use_cases: find which app is using all the CPU on my Mac
force quit a frozen or stuck application
monitor CPU and memory from the menu bar
quiet down a runaway Mac from the terminal
check per-process network speed on macOS
how_to_run: xcodebuild -project MacResourceMonitor.xcodeproj -scheme MacResourceMonitor -configuration Release -destination 'platform=macOS' -derivedDataPath build/DerivedData build
notable: Ends processes directly from the menu bar table, with system services shown but protected from being killed
Command-line 'mrm doom' mode previews and quiets your own non-system processes, always keeping the terminal chain, the monitor, and Finder
Freeze toggle keeps row order stable while numbers update; hovering End pins a row so refreshes do not shift the click target
Shows human app names (e.g. ChatGPT rather than node) and includes Apple apps in the one-click end list
Stays local: no account, no telemetry, MIT licensed
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later; not available for Windows or Linux
The menu bar icon cannot be hidden, and a small recovery window appears after hiding it
Not a sensor dashboard or process tree; sensors, dock icon, Mac App Store and sandboxed builds are explicitly out of scope
